text:
Microsoft's Recall feature became a privacy scandal in 2024 because, despite claims of encryption, security researchers demonstrated that the screenshots it captured every few seconds were stored unencrypted (in plaintext) within a local SQLite database [Source: ev-1]. This storage method allowed any process running as the user to access sensitive content visible on screen, including passwords and private messages, by default [Source: ev-1]. The discrepancy between Microsoft’s "encrypted" claims and the actual insecure implementation, combined with the default-on nature of recording everything on screen—including health data—created a major collision with privacy expectations [Source: ev-1].

In response to this controversy and inquiries from regulators such as the Irish Data Protection Commission and the UK Information Commissioner's Office, Microsoft changed the feature significantly [Source: ev-1]. Initially delayed in June 2024, Recall was relaunched as an opt-in feature (default OFF) rather than being enabled automatically [Source: ev-1]. Additionally, access to the timeline now requires Windows Hello authentication and presence detection, while incognito and DRM content are explicitly excluded from capture [Source: ev-1]. The revised version reached general availability on Copilot+ PCs in 2025 [Source: ev-1].
